monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-three, crowded and heavy. I press the tired wedge down on the Leaning Box, leaning hard into this heat until the flat rock stops its lazy slide. The thin tree I set there presses on the flat line now, and I wonder if it is too much. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under. Is the air above the card heavy, like a lid, or just empty space pressing down? If they say empty, I will build a lid out of the idea of weight. I touch the box again, swapping a tall tree for a flat grass stone to make room for this thin shape. The air feels thick as wet paper, pressing on a fence that hasn't slid yet. I hope the slip waits.

action.why: The flat line still feels too thin to hold the heat, so I will press down harder on the wedge again.

recalled.text: Your diary: "I went to tend The Slip Waits, but found only the Tall Fence standing there like a ghost."
Your diary: "I drew a rough corner to catch the dot, but the lines shake like a tired leg while the cool air tries to swell the memory."
Something you no longer remember: "The tall rock leans too much, yet the slip waits."
